# 玉清胎元內養真經

**ID:** KR5a0063
**Custom ID:** ZB5a0063

**Editions:** SJB, ZHDZ

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A three-folio scripture transmitted (as its opening states) by Yuántái zhēnjūn 元胎真君 — a name also mentioned in *[DZ 42 Yùqīng yuánshǐ xuánhuáng jiǔguāng zhēnjīng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0042)* 2b. The scripture preserves the instruction of Yuánshǐ shàngdì 元始上帝 to propagate methods for restoring one's original vital forces, which consist in enriching one's immanent *qì* with the cosmic "true spirit" (*zhēnshén* 真神). In terms of individual practice, this means concentration of the mind (*dìngxīn* 定心), shutting out external distractions (alcohol, sex), and restriction of inner ambitions and thoughts. By observing first the small and then the great precepts (*xiǎojiè* 小戒 / *dàjiè* 大戒), the adept finally attains the state of non-acting (*wúwéi* 無為). By multiplying their persons (*fēnshēn* 分身), Tàishàng Lǎojūn 太上老君 and Zǐguāng tiānmǔ 紫光天母 ensure the diffusion of the scripture and the salvation of innumerable beings, who in their turn promise in a hymn to continue the work of salvation (compare *[DZ 64 Yùqīng wúshàng nèijīng zhēnjīng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0064)*).

**Abstract**

Ursula-Angelika Cedzich, in Schipper & Verellen eds., *The Taoist Canon* (2004) 2:1233 (§3.B.14, "Other Popular Cults"), treats the scripture as belonging to the mid-to-late Sòng Daoist cultivation literature associated with the Zǐguāng tiānmǔ 紫光天母 cult (the goddess of the Northern Dipper from whom, in the cognate scriptures, the Nine Luminaries proceed). The frontmatter brackets composition notBefore 1100 / notAfter 1279, with dynasty 宋. No author is attributed.
